# Visualizing Distributions

## Distributions

- How a particular variable is distributed in a dataset
- Statistics: Mean, median, mode, standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis
- Visualizations: Histogram, density plot, boxplot, violin plot

## Histograms

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Filled rectangles
- Bin = Width of rectangle = range of values in that bin
- Height of rectangle = number of observations or proportion of whole in that bin
- Bin width matters for storytelling

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-hist", fig_hist(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Density plots

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Curve estimated from the data - smooth version of a histogram
- Area under the curve = 1
- Height of curve = density of observations at that value
- Density interpretation: Probability of observing a value in a given range = area under the curve for that range
- Bandwidth matters for storytelling

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-density", fig_density(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Density plots
:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Pitfall: smooth across gaps in data or where there are no observations.

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-density-bad", fig_density_bad(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```


## Two distributions

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Avoid stacked histograms - hard to compare values
- Bars start at different points
- Use side-by-side histograms or density plots instead

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-stacked-histogram", fig_stacked_histogram(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 9.5, y = 1.5, width = 4.3)
place_fig("fig_side-histogram", fig_side_histogram(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 9.5, y = 5.0, width = 4.3)
```

## Two distributions

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Avoid stacked histograms - hard to compare values
- Bars start at different points
- Use side-by-side histograms or density plots instead

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-two-density", fig_two_density(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## More than two distributions

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Density plots extend nicely to more than one distribution
- Use color to separate distributions
- Transparency can help with overlapping distributions

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-four-density", fig_four_density(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Quantile--quantile (Q-Q) plots

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Compare observed data to a reference distribution (usually normal)
- Rank each point, then plot its observed value vs. the value expected at that rank
- Diagonal line = *x* equals *y*
- Points on the line: data follow the reference distribution

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-student-grades-qq", fig_student_grades_qq(),
          w = 4, h = 3.9, x = 9, y = 1.4, width = 6)
```


## Boxplots

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Divide the data into quartiles
- Line = median; box = middle 50% of the data (interquartile range)
- Whiskers extend to the most extreme points within the fences (1.5 × box height)
- Points beyond the fences = outliers

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-boxplot-schematic", fig_boxplot_schematic(),
          w = 7.1, h = 4.5, x = 7, y = 1.8, width = 8.5)
```

## Many distributions at once

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Boxplots: compact, easy to compare; show skew (e.g., December)
- Violin plots: mirrored density; reveal bimodality a boxplot hides (e.g., November)
- Violins inherit the shortcomings of density estimates

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-lincoln-temp-boxplots", fig_lincoln_temp_boxplots(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 9.5, y = 1.6, width = 4.2)
place_fig("fig-lincoln-temp-violins", fig_lincoln_temp_violins(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 9.5, y = 5.0, width = 4.2)
```

## Plotting all the points

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Strip chart: show every observation as a dot
- Overplotting hides which temperatures are most common
- Jittering spreads points along the *x* axis to show density
- Good option when the data are too sparse for violins

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-lincoln-temp-all-points", fig_lincoln_temp_all_points(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 9.5, y = 1.6, width = 4.2)
place_fig("fig-lincoln-temp-jittered", fig_lincoln_temp_jittered(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 9.5, y = 5.0, width = 4.2)
```
